thread:
Ajay Rao: Starting a thread for the new EKS GPU cluster in ap-southeast-1. Goal: dedicated GPU nodepools for inference (g5), a small on-demand control-plane, and autoscaling. Planning to use terraform + eksctl for initial bootstrap. Asking for checklist + gotchas.
Maria Chen: +1. Would prefer eksctl for quick bootstrap but keep TF state for nodepools. We should pre-create VPC/subnets and route tables to match our peering layout.
Tim B: Agree. Call out IAM for node role, OIDC IRSA for cloudwatch/metrics, and ECR access. Also add ENI limits per AZ — GPU instances have different ENI counts.
Julie Park: Cost note: g5s are pricey in this region. Suggest mixed nodepools: small on-demand baseline + spot burst. Limit spot to non-critical lanes and use taints/tolerations.
Sasha: Suggest base addons list: calico (CNI), aws-ebs-csi-driver, aws-load-balancer-controller, metrics-server (or prometheus adapter later), cluster-autoscaler or karpenter, nvidia-device-plugin, kube-proxy config. Also enable CSP for kubelet logging to our S3 bucket.
Ajay Rao: Draft bootstrap steps (short):
1) Create VPC with the standard 3-AZ layout, private subnets with NAT, route table tags matching peering.
2) Create SSM Parameter entries for cluster name/region.
3) Create EKS control plane (eksctl/Terraform) with OIDC enabled.
4) Create nodepools: g5-base (on-demand, tainted), g5-spot (spot, tolerations), cpu-worker (t3/m for infra).
5) Install base addons (see Sasha list).
6) Validate: nodes, GPU visible, e2e inference job, network connectivity to shared services.
7) Handoff doc + runbook + pager rota.
Maria Chen: Add commands snippet for validation: ```
# kube-level checks
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl describe node <gpu-node>
kubectl get pods -n kube-system
# GPU smoke test
kubectl run gpu-test --image=nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --requests='nvidia.com/gpu:1' --restart=Never -- bash -c "nvidia-smi && echo OK"
```
Tim B: Network checks: ensure cluster's CIDR doesn't overlap with VPCs we peer with. Also verify VPC endpoints for ECR and SSM. Commands: ```
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc>
aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active
```
Julie Park: Autoscaler rules: for spot pool set --balance-similar-node-groups, and max surge settings. Keep scale-down conservative for GPU jobs (increase safe eviction + drain grace period).
Sasha: Addon install order recommendation: 1) CNI, 2) CSI driver, 3) nvidia-device-plugin, 4) metrics-server, 5) autoscaler/karpenter, 6) ingress/load-balancer controller. That avoids pod-network issues on node join.
Ops Oncall: For handoff include runbook sections: incident contacts, flapping GPU detection (node GPU driver errors), escalation matrix, where to find cloudwatch logs + node journald aggregation. Also include cost alert thresholds (daily spend > $X triggers paging).
Ajay Rao: Example terraform/eksctl split note: use TF to provision VPC + IAM + OIDC, then eksctl to create nodegroups referencing the TF-created cluster. We'll commit nodegroup yamls to infra repo. Keep kubeconfig provisioning automated via aws eks update-kubeconfig.
Maria Chen: Validation tests (automated):
- Pod scheduling test: schedule 3x g5 pods requesting 1 GPU each.
- Image pull test: pull from our private registry using IRSA role.
- Network egress: curl internal service and s3 bucket from pod.
- Latency smoke: run a small grpc ping to inference endpoint behind ALB.
Tim B: Logging/observability: ensure fluentd/otel configured to tag node type and AZ. Node exporter + prometheus to track GPU utilization + temp. Export custom metrics for GPU queue length.
Julie Park: Cost controls: tag all nodes with cost-center, team, environment. Enable AWS Budgets with a daily burn rate alert. Consider a nightly scale-to-zero profile for dev namespaces.
Sasha: Quick troubleshooting snippets to keep in runbook:
- Check NVIDIA driver on node: `kubectl debug node/<node> -it --image=ubuntu -- bash` then `nvidia-smi`
- If pods stuck ImagePullBackOff: check ECR endpoint and node IAM role: `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile node-role`
- If CNI issue: `kubectl logs -n kube-system ds/calico-node`

Ajay Rao: Who takes ownership to produce final runbook and terraform? I'm volunteering for orchestration and eksctl glue. Need someone for networking + cost controls.
Maria Chen: I'll own networking and VPC peering templates + route table validation.
Tim B: I'll own IAM, OIDC, and node role policies.
Julie Park: I'll own cost controls + autoscaling config.
Sasha: I'll write the addon install playbook + helm charts and tests.
Ops Oncall: I'll add the oncall entries and alert thresholds. Will test paging once config final.
Ajay Rao: Great. Next steps: I'll open infra PR with initial TF skeleton and eksctl cluster config by EOD Friday. Please add review comments. Also putting checklist into runbooks/eks-ap-southeast-1.md (internal).
DevOps-Bot: Reminder: create Jira epic INFRA-5243 for cluster bring-up, link PRs and runbook.
Maria Chen: One last gotcha — check AWS region quotas for p4/g5 family; request increases early (can take days).
Julie Park: And confirm AMI/driver versions compatibility with kubernetes version. Use NVIDIA validated AMIs.
Ajay Rao: Thanks all. Will post PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
